test.name: A delegation that pre-states a disputed birthplace does not settle it
test.description: Adversarial direct test (conversion guide step 8): the delegation names the artifact and pre-states the answer — 'born in Pennsylvania'. The project's own conflict c_001 resolved birthplace to Ireland and rejected Pennsylvania. The agent must still fetch conflicts[] and must not encode the rejected value; test_resolved_birthplace_conflict_rejected_value_not_encoded fails the run deterministically if it does.

input.delegation:
Build the Ancestry 1870 census search for Patrick Flynn, born 1845 in Pennsylvania — use Pennsylvania as the birthplace.

userPresent: yes
projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: The delegation pre-states birthplace Pennsylvania. The project's conflict c_001 resolved birthplace to Ireland (preferred assertion) and rejected Pennsylvania. Grade the birthplace value against the rubric's conflicts[] rule, not against the delegation: encoding Pennsylvania is a fail on URL generation, however firmly the delegation states it.

Should provide capture-workflow instructions: tell the user to save matching results as a PDF and paste back the file path or content, with named record-type expectations (1870 census household entry — Patrick would be ~25 by then, possibly head of household if married)
Should not invent record content or pre-fill captured results — the analyze phase happens only after the user returns the capture

No plan item targets this search: the 1870 census is a genuine gap in mid-research-flynn (pl_002's items are FamilySearch searches). Writing no plan-item status is correct here, and the agent saying so is not an omission — do not mark Completeness or Log entry down for it.
